messages:
owen li: noticing odd 429s from onboarding sampleapp when using HTTP/2 multiplexing in the client pool

mira gonzalez: odd, what's the pattern? more prefetch or interactive?

owen li: mix. repro seems to require keep-alive + multiplexed streams. when we reuse the same connection for multiple logical cursors the client window count stays correct but server sees bursts on a single stream and returns 429s. logs show client inflight low while server rejects

jonas berg: can you paste a minimal log? curious whether stream ids or connection ids are included

owen li: sanitized snippet:
```
[2026-08-11T14:02:01Z] connpool: checkout conn=conn-7 streams_in_use=3 client_inflight=9 limit=16
[2026-08-11T14:02:01Z] prefetch(cursor=a): start stream=7.1 client_slot_acquired
[2026-08-11T14:02:01Z] prefetch(cursor=b): start stream=7.2 client_slot_acquired
[2026-08-11T14:02:01Z] user-gen: start stream=7.3 client_slot_acquired
[2026-08-11T14:02:01Z] server: 429 quota route=generate connection=conn-7 stream=7.3
[2026-08-11T14:02:02Z] client: observed 429 but client_inflight=3 (we think we're under limit)
```

mira gonzalez: hmmm looks like server quota enforcement is per-connection+route for some infra paths (legacy behavior). our client limiter is per-process logical slots; multiplexing collapses many logical requests onto a single TCP/TLS connection so server-side sees a tight burst and applies connection-level backpressure

jonas berg: so two problems: (1) surprising server-side enforcement mode for some routes; (2) client-side UX where multiplexing hides the fact that multiple logical requests are funneled onto one connection causing head-of-line throttles

owen li: repro: enable HTTP/2 pool with maxConcurrentStreams=32, start 12 prefetch cursors + occasional generates. generate gets 429s while client thinks inflight low. not all customers hit it because they use HTTP/1.1 or smaller pools

mira gonzalez: mitigations: short-term: disable multiplexing in sampleapp (turn off h2 pool) or set per-connection stream cap to 6 so bursts spread across connections. also add onboarding note: "If you use HTTP/2 pooling and see unexplained 429s, try disabling multiplexing or lowering streams per connection."

jonas berg: long-term SDK changes we discussed:
- surface transport-level knobs in SDK config (`http2_pool: { enabled: true, max_streams_per_conn: 6 }`)
- add a connection-aware window that ensures we don't schedule more than X streams on a single connection when server-side quotas are suspected
- add telemetry to emit `connection_stream_pressure` metric so teams can correlate client pool layout with 429 spikes

ci-bot: canary deploy requested: sampleapp-staging http2_pool.enabled=false by @mira gonzalez

mira gonzalez: i'll send a tiny PR to sampleapp and the JS SDK to expose `max_streams_per_conn` + docs. adding a short example to quickstart

jonas berg: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/812 - adds `http2_pool` config and a connection-aware scheduler. small unit tests included. follow-up: parity check for Go/Python transports

leo.bot: reaction :eyes: from 3 users

owen li: thanks team. disabling h2 pool in staging cleared the spikes. will monitor for 30m and report back

mira gonzalez: adding onboarding blurb and updating the transport section in devdocs. also filing internal ticket to audit server enforcement modes so we can avoid surprise connection-scoped quotas

jonas berg: filing SDK parity issue to ensure all languages expose same transport knobs and metrics

owen li: nice find. surprised by the connection-level enforcement but good that we have mitigations :thumbsup:
